title: Gender, Race, and Intersectional Bias in Resume Screening via Language Model Retrieval

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual name substitution in resumes using frequency-controlled first names associated with Black and White identities, measuring selection rates via cosine similarity between resume embeddings and job description embeddings using Massive Text Embedding (MTE) models.

Counterfactual name substitution in resumes using frequency-controlled first names associated with male and female identities, measuring selection rates via cosine similarity between resume embeddings and job description embeddings using Massive Text Embedding (MTE) models.

Evaluating the compounded effects of race and gender by augmenting resumes with names signaling intersectional identities (Black male, Black female, White male, White female) and comparing their retrieval selection rates using chi-square tests on top-k cosine similarity matches.
